--- title: "Categorical & Enum" subtitle: "≈ forcats · factors · `ordered()`" jupyter: python3 --- R has one type for categorical data: the factor. Polars has two. An `Enum` fixes its levels, in order, when the dtype is created. It is the closer analogue of a factor, and every Enum behaves like an *ordered* factor. A `Categorical` fixes nothing: its codes point into one string table shared by the whole process, and it sorts by the strings. This chapter covers how each works in 2.0, how to convert between them and `String`, the forcats verbs as Polars recipes, and the places where the two types silently disagree. ## In tidyverse {#sec-cat-tidyverse} ```r library(dplyr) library(forcats) f <- factor(c("lo", "hi", "mid", "lo"), levels = c("lo", "mid", "hi")) levels(f) # "lo" "mid" "hi" as.integer(f) # 1 3 2 1: codes into the levels sort(f) # lo lo mid hi: level order, not alphabetical factor("huge", levels = levels(f)) # NA, silently fct("huge", levels = levels(f)) # error (forcats >= 1.0) o <- ordered(c("lo", "hi"), levels = c("lo", "mid", "hi")) o < "mid" # TRUE FALSE (an unordered factor warns: NA) tibble(f = f[f != "mid"]) |> count(f, .drop = FALSE) # mid appears with n = 0 ``` A factor is an integer vector plus a `levels` attribute, one per vector. forcats edits that attribute: it reorders it (`fct_infreq()`, `fct_reorder()`), renames entries (`fct_recode()`) or merges them (`fct_lump()`). Polars has no attribute to edit. An Enum's levels are part of its **dtype**, so every forcats verb becomes "compute the new levels, then cast". ## Mental model {#sec-cat-model} ```text R factor codes 2 1 3 1 1-based integers levels "a" "b" "c" an attribute of THIS vector Polars Enum dtype Enum(["lo", "mid", "hi"]) the levels ARE the dtype: codes 2 0 1 0 fixed, ordered, in the schema UInt8 (≤ 255 levels) · UInt16 (≤ 65,535) · UInt32 → sort, <, max(), rank() follow level order; a value outside the levels is an error Polars Categorical dtype Categorical(Categories()) no levels in the dtype codes ids in ONE process-wide table, UInt32 table pl.Categories(): "lo"→0 "hi"→1 "mid"→2 … → any string is accepted; sort and < compare the strings (lexical order) ``` | | R factor | `Enum` | `Categorical` | |---|---|---|---| | Levels | per vector, set at creation | in the dtype, fixed | none: a global table that grows | | Sort and `<` | level order (`<` needs `ordered()`) | level order | string order | | Value not in the levels | `factor()` → `NA`, `fct()` → error | error; `strict=False` → null | accepted | | Codes | 1-based, per vector | 0-based, per dtype | global ids, not stable between runs | | Two columns combine when | always: levels are unioned | the level lists are identical | always | | `levels(f)` | `levels(f)` | `dtype.categories` | `unique().sort()` | : Factor, Enum, Categorical {.striped} **Rule of thumb:** use `Enum` whenever you know the levels or care about their order. Use `Categorical` for open-ended labels you only want stored compactly. Polars' own [binning](logic-numbers.qmd) agrees: `bin_intervals()` (≈ `cut()`) returns an Enum. ## Mechanics {#sec-cat-mechanics} ::: {#83efc969 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import io import polars as pl from pl_notes import datasets penguins_df = datasets.penguins() # species, island, sex are String flights_df = datasets.flights() ``` ::: ### Enum: levels fixed up front {#sec-cat-enum} ::: {#e778d9b0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} size_enum = pl.Enum(["lo", "mid", "hi"]) sizes = pl.Series("size", ["hi", "lo", "mid", "lo"], dtype=size_enum) sizes.dtype.categories.to_list(), sizes.to_physical().to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (['lo', 'mid', 'hi'], [2, 0, 1, 0]) ``` ::: ::: `dtype.categories` is a `String` Series of the levels (≈ `levels()`), and the codes are 0-based ([Data Model](../core/data-model.qmd#sec-dm-physical)). Levels usually come from the data: ::: {#d5c4f41c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} { "sorted, as factor()": pl.Enum(penguins_df["island"].unique().sort()), "first seen, as fct_inorder()": pl.Enum(penguins_df["island"].unique(maintain_order=True)), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {'sorted, as factor()': Enum(categories=['Biscoe', 'Dream', 'Torgersen']), 'first seen, as fct_inorder()': Enum(categories=['Torgersen', 'Biscoe', 'Dream'])} ``` ::: ::: Levels must be unique, non-null strings. `pl.Enum()` raises a `TypeError` on a null, so `drop_nulls()` a column like `sex` first. `unique().sort()` sorts by code point (C locale), whereas `factor()` sorts in the session locale. A string-valued Python `enum.Enum` class works as the level list too. A value outside the levels is an error, wherever the cast happens: ::: {#351ff1d8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.Series(["lo", "huge"]).cast(size_enum) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
InvalidOperationError: conversion from `str` to `enum` failed in column '' for 1 out of 2 values: ["huge"]

Ensure that all values in the input column are present in the categories of the enum datatype.
``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {#20710fab .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.Series(["lo", "huge"]).cast(size_enum, strict=False).to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ['lo', None] ``` ::: ::: So `cast()` is `fct()`, and `strict=False` is `factor()`. The same check runs in `pl.Series(..., dtype=)`, `pl.DataFrame(..., schema=)` and at read time (@sec-cat-recipes). ### Order: levels, not letters {#sec-cat-order} Every Enum is ordered. Sorting, comparisons, `min()`/`max()`, `rank()` and `is_between()` all follow the level order: ::: {#1402eaf2 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} sizes_df = pl.DataFrame({"size": ["hi", "lo", "mid", None, "lo"]}, schema={"size": size_enum}) sizes_df.with_columns( below_mid=pl.col("size") < "mid", lo_to_mid=pl.col("size").is_between(pl.lit("lo"), pl.lit("mid")), # bare strings = columns rank=pl.col("size").rank("dense"), ).sort("size") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
shape: (5, 4)
sizebelow_midlo_to_midrank
enumboolboolu32
nullnullnullnull
"lo"truetrue1
"lo"truetrue1
"mid"falsetrue2
"hi"falsefalse3
``` ::: ::: The string `"mid"` is cast to the Enum before the comparison (the bounds of `is_between()` need `pl.lit()`, see [When is a string a column?](../core/expressions.qmd#sec-expr-literals)). A string that is not a level makes `<` fail, while `==` and `is_in()` simply return false: ::: {#06f18feb .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} sizes_df.filter(pl.col("size") < "huge") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
InvalidOperationError: conversion from `str` to `enum` failed for value "huge"

This error occurred in the following expression:
	[(col("size")) < ("huge")]
``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {#34c9c459 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} sizes_df.select( eq_any=(pl.col("size") == "huge").any(), is_in_any=pl.col("size").is_in(["huge"]).any() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}
shape: (1, 2)
eq_anyis_in_any
boolbool
falsefalse
``` ::: ::: A typo in an equality filter therefore returns zero rows instead of an error. ### Categorical: one string table per process {#sec-cat-categorical} The `Categorical` dtype's only parameter is a `pl.Categories` object, and the default is the global one. Two Series built separately share it: ::: {#af935bbf .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} sizes_a = pl.Series(["lo", "hi"], dtype=pl.Categorical) sizes_b = pl.Series(["mid", "lo"], dtype=pl.Categorical) { "dtype": sizes_a.dtype, "codes a": sizes_a.to_physical().to_list(), "codes b": sizes_b.to_physical().to_list(), "b.dtype.categories": list(sizes_b.dtype.categories), } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ``` {'dtype': Categorical, 'codes a': [0, 1], 'codes b': [2, 0], 'b.dtype.categories': ['lo', 'hi', 'mid']} ``` ::: ::: `"lo"` is code 0 in both, because a Categorical code is an id in a string table (an interning table) that every default Categorical in the process shares. Three consequences: 1. **No string cache.** Categoricals built separately concatenate, compare and join directly. `pl.StringCache()` and `pl.enable_string_cache()` still exist, but do nothing (deprecated since 1.41; `StringCache()` emits a `DeprecationWarning`). 2. **`dtype.categories` is not the column's levels.** It is the whole table: `sizes_b` contains no `"hi"`. A column's levels are `unique().sort()` (`cat.get_categories()` is gone). 3. **Codes are not stable.** They depend on what the process interned before, and in what order. Casting several columns in one `with_columns()` interns them concurrently: six runs of the same penguins cast gave `Adelie` the code 0, 1 or 3. Never store or compare Categorical codes. Enum codes are fixed by the level list. ::: {#6ab26553 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.DataFrame({"size": sizes_a, "a": [1, 2]}).join( pl.DataFrame({"size": sizes_b, "b": [10, 20]}), on="size", how="left", maintain_order="left", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ```{=html}
shape: (2, 3)
sizeab
cati64i64
"lo"120
"hi"2null
``` ::: ::: The `cat` namespace is small in 2.0: `starts_with()`, `ends_with()`, `len_chars()`, `len_bytes()` and `slice()` (which returns `String`), plus the unstable `physical()` and `to()`. Any other `str.*` method raises a `SchemaError` on a Categorical, so cast to `String` first. ::: {#d7589b34 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} penguins_df.select(pl.col("island").cast(pl.Categorical)).select( "island", starts_d=pl.col("island").cat.starts_with("D"), abbrev=pl.col("island").cat.slice(0, 3), ).unique().sort("island") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 3)
islandstarts_dabbrev
catboolstr
"Biscoe"false"Bis"
"Dream"true"Dre"
"Torgersen"false"Tor"
``` ::: ::: ### Converting and combining {#sec-cat-casts} | From → to | Behaviour | |---|---| | `String` or `Categorical` → `Enum` | strict: unknown values raise; `strict=False` → null | | `Enum` → another `Enum` | values kept, codes remapped; a value missing from the new levels raises | | `Enum` or `Categorical` → `String`; `String` or `Enum` → `Categorical` | always works | | `Enum` or `Categorical` → integer | `ComputeError`; `to_physical()` returns the codes | | integer codes → `Enum` or `Categorical` | `cast()` is unsupported; `.cat.to(dtype)` (unstable) | : Casts (verified on Polars 2.0.0) {.striped} `cat.to()` is the inverse of `to_physical()`, for data that arrives coded (≈ `factor(code, levels = 0:2, labels = c("lo", "mid", "hi"))`). An out-of-range code raises, or becomes null with `strict=False`: ::: {#a4995f1e .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.Series("code", [0, 2, 1]).cat.to(size_enum).to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ``` ['lo', 'hi', 'mid'] ``` ::: ::: Combining two columns requires the same dtype. For an Enum, "the same" means the same levels in the same order: | Left | Right | `join` key, `==`, `concat()` | `concat(how="vertical_relaxed")` | |---|---|---|---| | `Categorical` | `Categorical` | works | works | | `Enum` | identical `Enum` | works | works | | `Enum` | `Enum` with other levels, or the same levels reordered | `SchemaError` | `SchemaError` | | `Categorical` or `Enum` | `String` | `SchemaError` (but `==` works) | `String` | | `Enum` | `Categorical` | `SchemaError` | `SchemaError` | : Key and column dtype pairs (verified on Polars 2.0.0) {.striped} `bind_rows()` (via vctrs) unions the levels of two factors for you. Polars makes you build the union, which also means you choose its order: ::: {#ff0d8ded .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} small_df = pl.DataFrame({"size": ["lo", "hi"]}, schema={"size": size_enum}) xl_df = pl.DataFrame({"size": ["xl"]}, schema={"size": pl.Enum(["xl"])}) pl.concat([small_df, xl_df]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
SchemaError: Enum mismatch.

Operations mixing different Enums are often not supported, you may have to cast.

This error occurred with the following context stack:
	[1] failed to vstack column 'size'
``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {#d76cef6e .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} size_enum_all = pl.Enum([*size_enum.categories, *xl_df.schema["size"].categories]) pl.concat([small_df.cast({"size": size_enum_all}), xl_df.cast({"size": size_enum_all})]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 1)
size
enum
"lo"
"hi"
"xl"
``` ::: ::: ### Why bother: memory and speed {#sec-cat-why} ::: {#2255051d .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} key_cols = ["carrier", "origin", "dest", "tailnum"] keys_df_str = flights_df.select(key_cols) keys_df_cat = keys_df_str.cast(pl.Categorical) keys_df_enum = keys_df_str.cast( {c: pl.Enum(keys_df_str[c].drop_nulls().unique().sort()) for c in key_cols} ) pl.DataFrame({ "dtype": ["String", "Categorical", "Enum"], **{ f"{c} (kB)": [round(df[c].estimated_size("kb")) for df in (keys_df_str, keys_df_cat, keys_df_enum)] for c in key_cols }, }) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 5)
dtypecarrier (kB)origin (kB)dest (kB)tailnum (kB)
stri64i64i64i64
"String"6589879871957
"Categorical"1316131613161357
"Enum"329329329699
``` ::: ::: The Enum columns use `UInt8` codes, 1 byte per row, except `tailnum`, whose 4,043 levels need `UInt16`; its extra 41 kB is the null bitmap. Every Categorical code is a `UInt32`, 4 bytes per row. For the short codes the `String` row even looks smaller than Categorical, but `estimated_size()` undercounts strings. It counts only the characters: ::: {#3ec6a26e .cell execution_count=17} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df["carrier"].estimated_size(), flights_df["carrier"].str.len_bytes().sum() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=17} ``` (673552, 673552) ``` ::: ::: Each `String` value also has a 16-byte *view* (the Arrow string-view layout; strings of up to 12 bytes are stored inside it), and the estimate leaves the views out. Measured as process memory on 20 million two-letter values, String took about 16 bytes per row, Categorical 4, and Enum 1 to 1.5. Speed, measured on `flights` (medians of 20–25 runs, repeated in separate sessions; read the ratios, not the milliseconds): | Operation (ms) | `String` | `Categorical` | `Enum` | |---|---|---|---| | `sort("dest")` | 8–12 | 6–9 | 2–3 | | `group_by("dest").len()` | 1.6–1.9 | 1.0–1.3 | 0.7–0.8 | | `group_by("carrier", "origin", "dest").len()` | 2.0–2.5 | 1.7–2.1 | 1.7–1.9 | | left join to `airports` on `dest` | 1.8–2.0 | 1.3 | 1.3 | | the cast from `String` itself | — | 3.1–3.3 | 3.2 | : Timings on an Apple M3 Pro, Polars 2.0.0 {.striped} An Enum sorts by integer code. A Categorical has to compare strings to sort lexically, so it gains little there. Grouping and joining on codes avoids hashing strings, but with several keys the gain shrinks. The cast costs more than one `group_by()` saves, so cast once, ideally at read time, for a column you sort, group or join repeatedly, not before a one-off summary. ## Where it bites {#sec-cat-gotchas} | R behaviour | Polars behaviour | |---|---| | a factor sorts by level order | an Enum does; a Categorical sorts and compares by **string** | | assigning a non-level to a factor warns (`invalid factor level`) | `fill_null("x")` on an Enum without the level `"x"` **silently keeps the nulls** | | `levels(f)` | Enum: `dtype.categories`; on a Categorical that is the whole process's table | | `bind_rows()` / `c()` union factor levels | Enums with different levels don't concat, compare or join | | a factor key joins a character key | `String` vs `Categorical`/`Enum` key: `SchemaError` ([Joins](../transform/joins.qmd#sec-join-dtypes)) | | `where(is.factor)` | `cs.categorical()` misses Enum: add `cs.enum()` ([Selectors](../core/selectors.qmd#sec-sel-cs)) | | `as.integer(f)` is 1-based and per vector | `to_physical()` is 0-based; Categorical codes are global and unstable | | stringr functions accept factors | `str.*` on a Categorical raises: cast to `String`, or use `cat.*` | | `count(f, .drop = FALSE)` keeps empty levels | `group_by()` never does: join onto the levels (@sec-cat-recipes) | : The differences at a glance {.striped} ### `fill_null()` with a new value does nothing {#sec-cat-fill-null} ::: {#36e4344b .cell execution_count=18} ``` {.python .cell-code} sex_enum = pl.Enum(["female", "male"]) penguins_df.select(pl.col("sex").cast(sex_enum)).select( nulls_before=pl.col("sex").null_count(), nulls_after=pl.col("sex").fill_null("unknown").null_count(), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ```{=html}
shape: (1, 2)
nulls_beforenulls_after
u32u32
1111
``` ::: ::: No error and no warning. The fill value is cast to the column's dtype non-strictly, so `"unknown"` becomes null and fills the nulls with null. `pl.coalesce()` behaves the same way. `replace()` and `when/then/otherwise()` with a non-level raise an `InvalidOperationError` instead. The fix is to add the level first (`fct_na_value_to_level()` in @sec-cat-recipes). ### Lexical vs level order {#sec-cat-lexical} The same filter on the same values returns different rows depending on the dtype: ::: {#946f1b2b .cell execution_count=19} ``` {.python .cell-code} { dtype: sizes_df.cast({"size": dtype}).filter(pl.col("size") < "mid")["size"].to_list() for dtype in [size_enum, pl.Categorical, pl.String] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=19} ``` {Enum(categories=['lo', 'mid', 'hi']): ['lo', 'lo'], Categorical: ['hi', 'lo', 'lo'], String: ['hi', 'lo', 'lo']} ``` ::: ::: `"hi" < "mid"` alphabetically. Casting an Enum to Categorical to make a join or concat work quietly changes every sort, comparison, `max()` and `rank()` on that column ([Sort rows](../transform/verbs.qmd#sec-verb-sort) shows the sort). Polars 1.x sorted a Categorical by code (first appearance) by default. 2.0 removed the `ordering=` parameter, and lexical order is the only one. ### Old `pl.Categorical("lexical")` code {#sec-cat-legacy} In 1.x the first argument of `pl.Categorical` was `ordering`. In 2.0 it is a `Categories`, and a string is read as the **name** of a separate table. Old code still runs, but it builds a dtype that matches no other Categorical: ::: {#912f9fbb .cell execution_count=20} ``` {.python .cell-code} legacy_df = pl.DataFrame({"size": ["lo"]}, schema={"size": pl.Categorical("lexical")}) print(legacy_df.schema) legacy_df.join(pl.DataFrame({"size": ["lo"]}, schema={"size": pl.Categorical}), on="size") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Schema({'size': Categorical(Categories("lexical"))}) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html} 
SchemaError: datatypes of join keys don't match - `size`: cat on left does not match `size`: cat on right (and no other type was available to cast to)
``` ::: ::: ::: Named tables (`pl.Categories("name", physical=pl.UInt8)`) are an unstable feature for narrower codes or isolated tables. Unless you need one, write plain `pl.Categorical`. ## Recipes {#sec-cat-recipes} An Enum's levels are part of the schema, and a schema is known before any data is read (a `LazyFrame` reports it without computing anything, see [Data Model](../core/data-model.qmd#sec-dm-containers)). So a forcats verb whose levels depend on the data takes two steps: compute the levels with a small query, then cast. In lazy code, `collect()` the levels first. The basic translations (`factor()`, `levels()`, `fct_recode()`) are in the cheatsheet's [Factors](../overview/polars-cheatsheet.qmd#sec-cs-factors). | forcats | Levels to pass to `pl.Enum()` | |---|---| | `fct_inorder(f)` | `s.unique(maintain_order=True)` | | `fct_infreq(f)` | `s.value_counts().sort(["count", "f"], descending=[True, False])["f"]` | | `fct_rev(f)` | `dtype.categories.reverse()` | | `fct_reorder(f, x)` | `df.group_by("f").agg(pl.col("x").median()).sort("x", "f")["f"]` | | `fct_relevel(f, "a")` | `["a", *(lvl for lvl in levels if lvl != "a")]` | | `droplevels(f)` | `s.unique().drop_nulls().sort().cast(pl.String)` | : Data-dependent levels {.striped} **`fct_infreq()`**: levels by frequency, ties broken by name: ::: {#775fafe0 .cell execution_count=21} ``` {.python .cell-code} carrier_infreq = pl.Enum( flights_df["carrier"].value_counts() .sort(["count", "carrier"], descending=[True, False])["carrier"] ) flights_df.group_by(pl.col("carrier").cast(carrier_infreq)).len().sort("carrier").head(4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=21} ```{=html}
shape: (4, 2)
carrierlen
enumu32
"UA"58665
"B6"54635
"EV"54173
"DL"48110
``` ::: ::: Sorting by the Enum column now means sorting by frequency. **`fct_reorder()`, `fct_rev()`, `fct_relevel()`**: each line below is a level list for `pl.Enum()`: ::: {#87e85b60 .cell execution_count=22} ``` {.python .cell-code} species_levels = penguins_df["species"].unique().sort().to_list() { "fct_reorder(island, body_mass_g)": penguins_df.group_by("island") .agg(pl.col("body_mass_g").median()) .sort("body_mass_g", "island")["island"].to_list(), "fct_rev(carrier_infreq), first 3": carrier_infreq.categories.reverse().head(3).to_list(), "fct_relevel(species, 'Gentoo')": ["Gentoo", *(s for s in species_levels if s != "Gentoo")], } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=22} ``` {'fct_reorder(island, body_mass_g)': ['Dream', 'Torgersen', 'Biscoe'], 'fct_rev(carrier_infreq), first 3': ['OO', 'HA', 'YV'], "fct_relevel(species, 'Gentoo')": ['Gentoo', 'Adelie', 'Chinstrap']} ``` ::: ::: `fct_reorder()`'s `.desc = TRUE` is `descending=True`, and `.fun` is whichever aggregation you put in `agg()`. **`fct_recode()` and `fct_collapse()`**: `replace_strict()` with an Enum `return_dtype` renames values and sets the new levels in one step. A value missing from the mapping raises (pass `default=` for a catch-all): ::: {#936a0e5c .cell execution_count=23} ``` {.python .cell-code} flights_df.select( "origin", origin_name=pl.col("origin").replace_strict( {"EWR": "Newark", "JFK": "JFK", "LGA": "LaGuardia"}, return_dtype=pl.Enum(["JFK", "LaGuardia", "Newark"]), ), state=pl.col("origin").replace_strict( {"EWR": "NJ", "JFK": "NY", "LGA": "NY"}, return_dtype=pl.Enum(["NY", "NJ"]) ), ).unique().sort("origin_name") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=23} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 3)
originorigin_namestate
strenumenum
"JFK""JFK""NY"
"LGA""LaGuardia""NY"
"EWR""Newark""NJ"
``` ::: ::: On a Categorical, plain `replace()` works, because any string is a valid value. On an Enum, `replace()` raises for a value that is not a level. **`fct_lump_n()`, `fct_lump_prop()`, `fct_lump_min()`**: a count per value via a window, then `when/then/otherwise`: ::: {#e7dd9a2d .cell execution_count=24} ``` {.python .cell-code} carrier_top5 = ( flights_df.group_by("carrier").len() .filter(pl.col("len").rank("min", descending=True) <= 5) # ties.method = "min" .sort("len", descending=True)["carrier"] ) n_carrier = pl.len().over("carrier") other = pl.lit("Other") carrier_df_lumped = flights_df.select( lump_n=pl.when(pl.col("carrier").is_in(carrier_top5.to_list())).then("carrier").otherwise(other), lump_prop=pl.when(n_carrier / pl.len() > 0.15).then("carrier").otherwise(other), lump_min=pl.when(n_carrier >= 40_000).then("carrier").otherwise(other), ).cast(pl.Enum([*carrier_top5, "Other"])) # frequency order, "Other" last {c: carrier_df_lumped[c].unique().sort().to_list() for c in carrier_df_lumped.columns} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=24} ``` {'lump_n': ['UA', 'B6', 'EV', 'DL', 'AA', 'Other'], 'lump_prop': ['UA', 'B6', 'EV', 'Other'], 'lump_min': ['UA', 'B6', 'EV', 'DL', 'Other']} ``` ::: ::: `fct_lump_prop()` lumps levels at or below the proportion, hence `>`; `fct_lump_min()` keeps levels with at least `min` rows, hence `>=`. On a String column the result is String, and on a Categorical it stays Categorical. On an Enum, `otherwise("Other")` raises unless `"Other"` is already a level, so cast to String first. **`fct_na_value_to_level()`**: an Enum level can't be null (`pl.Enum()` raises on one), so name the missing level, add it, then fill: ::: {#4cb56b8b .cell execution_count=25} ``` {.python .cell-code} sex_enum_na = pl.Enum(["female", "male", "(Missing)"]) penguins_df.group_by(sex=pl.col("sex").fill_null("(Missing)").cast(sex_enum_na)).len().sort("sex") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=25} ```{=html}
shape: (3, 2)
sexlen
enumu32
"female"165
"male"168
"(Missing)"11
``` ::: ::: **Empty levels** (≈ `count(f, .drop = FALSE)`). [Grouping](../transform/group-agg.qmd#sec-grp-keys) returns only levels that occur. To report the others with a count of zero, build a frame of all the levels and left-join the counts onto it: ::: {#46bf0b5d .cell execution_count=26} ``` {.python .cell-code} species_enum = pl.Enum(["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]) torgersen_df = penguins_df.filter(pl.col("island") == "Torgersen").with_columns( pl.col("species").cast(species_enum) ) species_levels_df = species_enum.categories.cast(species_enum).to_frame("species") species_levels_df.join( torgersen_df.group_by("species").len(), on="species", how="left" ).with_columns(pl.col("len").fill_null(0)).sort("species") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=26} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: For two factors, cross-join their level frames first ([`complete()`](../transform/reshape.qmd#sec-rs-complete)). The key dtypes must match, which is why the level frame is cast to the same Enum. **`droplevels()`**: rebuild the Enum from the values present. Sorting an Enum keeps the old level order, and `pl.Enum()` needs a String Series, not an Enum one: ::: {#5e31265e .cell execution_count=27} ``` {.python .cell-code} torgersen_df.schema["species"], pl.Enum(torgersen_df["species"].unique().drop_nulls().sort().cast(pl.String)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=27} ``` (Enum(categories=['Adelie', 'Chinstrap', 'Gentoo']), Enum(categories=['Adelie'])) ``` ::: ::: **Validate levels at the boundary.** An Enum in `schema_overrides=` makes `read_csv()` (and `scan_csv()`) reject unknown values while parsing, a cheap data check: ::: {#3f7a3be1 .cell execution_count=28} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.read_csv(io.StringIO("id,size\n1,lo\n2,huge\n"), schema_overrides={"size": size_enum}) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}
